items.titulo: Google Analytics adds two alerts for missing or malformed customer data
items.resumen: Codes e0 to e3 flag bad formats, old browsers, SHA256 failures and HTTP pages for GA4 advertisers. Google never says what PII rate sets off the low-rate alert.

items.titulo: Google lets a like stand in for 5 seconds of viewing in Shorts conversions
items.resumen: Comment and share taps also count as TrueView views, the unit cost-per-view advertisers pay for. Left open: when the rule began and what bidding makes of it.

items.titulo: Firms under 1,000 staff win GDPR records exemption in EU deal
items.resumen: Up from 250 staff now, the new line spares low-risk work but not firms that track people at scale as a core business. Will MEPs sign it off from November 23?

items.titulo: Lily Ray traces 23 years of Google warnings to one answer: real people
items.resumen: YouTube and Reddit hold 24.5% and 18.1% of top-50 AI Overview citations, data Ray cites for brands. Why does she think named experts outlast every SEO shortcut?

items.titulo: Turkey forces Google to let news sites exit AI Overviews but stay in search
items.resumen: News publishers also win non-discrimination and value-based terms under an October 8 interim order. What does that mean for Google's single AI opt-out toggle?

items.titulo: EU court adviser says "free" Facebook costs users their data
items.resumen: An EU court adviser said Facebook users pay with data, OpenAI tightened its rules for model resellers and Amazon set out its live shopping and deal guidance.

items.titulo: Free, at a price: EU court adviser says Facebook users pay in data
items.resumen: Ad-funded services that require sign-up data could not be called free under point 20 of the EU blacklist. Judges now weigh it before Germany's top court rules.

items.titulo: German top court halts Künast's fake quote case against Meta for EU ruling
items.resumen: Six questions now sit with EU judges, including whether feed algorithms strip Facebook of hosting protection. Will platforms have to vet reworded memes by hand?

items.titulo: OpenAI's research agents now finish 46% of two-to-four-hour tasks alone
items.resumen: Environment-building tasks succeed 29% of the time against 79% for monitoring, as median researcher agent spend hits $2,400 a day. Who still checks the work?

items.titulo: JudeLuxe lost a client two months in despite higher ROAS, Avery says
items.resumen: Unsold seasonal stock and cash short in the bank outweighed rising contribution for one ecommerce client. What PPC agencies now ask before accepting a target.

items.titulo: Bending Spoons buys growth by the billion, grows 3% on its own
items.resumen: Advertising revenue rose fivefold to $79m in Q3, and Mailchimp's roughly 1 million customers are next in line. Can borrowed money keep the buying spree going?

items.titulo: Texas says Character.ai's $10m sale can't move minors' data without parents
items.resumen: Eight conditions would bind buyer Smirks and Pangs, from ad opt-outs to no AI training on chats. Texas also wants the buyer's backer named before December 3.

items.titulo: 42 states and DC ask court to keep chats out of Character.ai's $10m sale
items.resumen: Therapist-bot transcripts, self-harm flags and 2.1 million minors' accounts head the states' list. Can a buyer formed a day before its pick take any of it?

items.titulo: Colorado bans ID-only age checks for AI chatbots in adopted rules
items.resumen: AI chatbot operators owe Colorado crisis-referral and age-check metrics by July 1, 2027. What still stands between these 76 pages of rules and enforcement?

items.titulo: PayPal faces possible clawback in Germany over its no-surcharge rule
items.resumen: German merchants have been barred since 2018 from charging PayPal users extra, so every shopper absorbs its fees. PayPal can respond before any final decision.

items.titulo: OpenAI patent describes earbuds that read silently mouthed words
items.resumen: Assistant users would mouth commands while ear-canal sensors read jaw motion at up to 1,000 Hz and feed language models. Can AI agents take orders no one hears?

items.titulo: Game: Your favourite marketing tool now answers to a new owner
items.resumen: Sixteen terms in four groups to start the week gently. One set comes from this week's coverage, and a couple of tiles look like they belong in your inbox.

items.titulo: New phrase-match searches cost 28% more per lead, New Path Digital finds
items.resumen: Phrase queries sharing no words with the keyword rose from 2% to 9% across three lead-gen accounts. New exact leads cost 7% less. What can three accounts prove?

items.titulo: Google AI Mode ads appear as deep as the fourth follow-up question
items.resumen: Sponsored phone and case carousels followed two turns of one conversation on November 6. US advertisers cannot opt out, and Google gives no per-turn reporting.

items.titulo: Google Ads counts a branded search as progress in a new journey card
items.resumen: Signed-in users only, eight days late: Performance Max, Search and Shopping advertisers get a four-stage card. Which campaign moved each user goes unreported.

items.titulo: Merchant Center sales running past 30 days may miss Google's sale badge
items.resumen: Discounts must sit between 5% and 90% in all 13 listed markets, with base price history rules on top. Google wrote "should", not "must": how firm is the line?

items.titulo: Google AI summary test says 4 Search advertisers are not browser tools
items.resumen: Semrush and three rivals were named in one AI sentence above mobile sponsored results, with AI notes under each ad. Who controls that copy, Google has not said.

items.titulo: Meta's website-crawling terms stay shelved into 2027 as publisher talks run
items.resumen: Three phases, an explainer document and a notice period come before any new terms bind advertisers. Which products are the revised terms written to enable?

items.titulo: Bing search ads show Zoro's 9.3 out of 10 Bizrate rating
items.resumen: Microsoft's rules name Bizrate and set a 30-review, 3.5-star bar for advertisers' merchant ratings. Microsoft has not said what, if anything, changed on Bing.

items.titulo: LinkedIn wants the business card to outlive the job
items.resumen: Only 27% of professionals regularly tend their network, LinkedIn data shows. Cards now sit in phone wallets. Can streak-based puzzles bring members back daily?

items.titulo: AppLovin blocks new ad lines in Google Ad Manager too, MonetizeMore CEO says
items.resumen: App publishers on Ad Manager keep only old AppLovin lines, at frozen floors. The 10-20% hybrid edge at stake is a vendor figure. An AppLovin analyst doubts it.

items.titulo: MGM+ brings ITV spy drama Secret Service to the US on November 22
items.resumen: ITV1 drew 3.9 million for episode one; MGM+ also takes Canada, Latin America and Italy. What changes when an ad-funded British hit lands on an ad-free service?

items.titulo: Most Prime Air drone orders arrive in under 90 minutes, Amazon says
items.resumen: Shoppers within 175 square miles of a site get items of 5 pounds or less, dropped from 13 feet. August's figure was 60 minutes. What else does the guide omit?
